title: Nicodemo Tranchedini and Boccaccino Alamanni, Florence, to Francesco Sforza, 27-29 Nov 1446 (BnF italien 1583 ff. 134, 139; DECODE R7905, R7908)

documents.route: Nicodemo Tranchedini da Pontremoli (Florence) -> Francesco Sforza

plaintext.source: contemporary interlinear glosses over most of the sign runs (small hand between the lines)

transcription.notes: No sign-by-sign transcription yet; about 60-70 signs in six or seven runs counted by eye.

documents.route: Boccaccino Alamanni and Nicodemo Tranchedini (Florence) -> Francesco Sforza

plaintext.source: no decipherment seen; the reply of 3 Dec 1446 (f. 147, clear) answers its matters and gives context, not a decipherment

transcription.notes: 778 signs on about 40 cipher-bearing lines, 240 (31%) unmatched shapes; two agents' labels not unified, so 172 distinct is an over-split; L21 dropped as a duplicate row of L22; L31-L33 may double-count.

system.summary: Graphic signs for letters (several signs for some letters), syllables, double letters and word signs (non, che, stantie, Fiorentini ...), written among clear Italian words; the key family of the later Tranchedini ciphers (Domnina 2018, Lasry 2026) is likely but unconfirmed for 1446.
system.sibling_key: possible: Domnina 2018 Fig. 5 (1454) and Lasry's 1452 table share the sign for non (confirmed by a gloss on f. 134); no 1446 key sheet known
system.notes: R7909, listed on the lead as f. 143, is the Duke's slip f. 145 (key R5323, see visconti1446), not Tranchedini's.

prior_solution.where: Searched 4 Nov 2026: Domnina 2018, Cipher Mysteries, Tomokiyo via the catalogue vetting, web search; no decipherment of ff. 134 or 139. Contemporary glosses on f. 134 only.

conditions.human_role: Posed the target from the catalogue page (pasted task, 4 Nov 2026); no target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: two Claude subagents for the sign transcription

solution.what: Images of R7905-R7910 taken from the it1583 worktree (DECODE); all five leaves viewed whole.
Identified the leaves: f. 135 and f. 147 are clear letters (no cipher); R7909 is the Duke's slip f. 145 in key R5323, not f. 143 of Tranchedini; the cipher is on f. 134 and f. 139 only.
Domnina 2018 (Fig. 5 extracted), Lasry's 1452 table, Cipher Mysteries and web search for the 1446 letters.
Read the interlinear glosses over f. 134's runs (gente d'arme in Toscana, alle stantie, fiorentini, non over the double-comb sign): the sign for non matches the later keys, and new word signs exist.
Tried Lasry's 1452 table on the first 12 signs of f. 139 line 3-4 by eye; no Italian came out.
f. 139 transcribed sign by sign by two subagents from 3-6x crops, labels from Domnina's and Lasry's tables, @NN for unmatched shapes: 778 signs, 172 labels, 31% unmatched.
Anchors from the clear context: ce-n-to-mi-l-a = cento mila before the clear 4m cavalli et 2m fanti; the comb sign = non; the bar-o-bar-o sign closes runs after 'la via' and 'l'impresa contra'.

Domnina/Lasry table values on 54 stretches (259 signs). First run (4 Nov) scored unspaced text with the spaced model (-3.91 vs -4.62, z 2.5): wrong. Corrected 5 Nov with it-cinquecento order 5 without spaces: -2.16 vs -3.04 (sd 0.23) for 200 shuffled assignments, z 3.9; real unspaced Italian about -1.8.

Replaced the two agents' hand labels by one automatic inventory: f. 139 deskewed 0.8 degrees, 41 text lines from projection peaks, glyph groups cut per line, 1080 narrow groups clustered (Ward, 90 clusters, contact sheets checked by eye). Measured texts/f139_seg.txt: 863 narrow signs in 73 types (against 172 labels before), IC 0.0177, 237 wide groups (clear words or linked signs) and 217 clear-text fragments still unseparated.

table_test2.py: 40 clusters mapped by eye to Domnina/Lasry values, 70 stretches (276 signs); corrected no-space model: -2.23 per letter vs -2.50 (sd 0.15) shuffled, z 1.8 (first run with the spaced model: z 2.2). Weaker than the agents' careful labels.

Partial decode of the agents' labelled lines with the table values and the clear words kept (texts/f139_partial_decode.txt): readable Italian stretches (o qui hauete che; cento mila; milia; et sforza; non in; et non per; o che pi ne da; Veneziani closing runs). Table letters largely right; the 31% unmatched shapes (nomenclator, syllables) missing.

solver.py: all 75 cluster types free on 691 signs, per-letter score under the no-space it-cinquecento model. Real -2.54, order shuffled -2.59, synthetic control (true key -2.32): solver -2.42, 1 of 53 types recovered. No power at this data size.

solver2.py: table values fixed for 455 of 788 tokens, 115 free types. Real -2.30 vs -2.51 to -2.60 shuffled; held-out control (free the 5 and 10 most frequent matched labels) restores 2/5 and 0/10 table values at the same score. Solver values for free labels are not evidence.

Read the top of f. 147 (R7910, Sforza's reply of 3 Dec): he answers their letter of 29 Nov, mainly on the money (dinaro) and the quarters (stantie), then Montevarchi (about 3500 horse). Confirms the topic of f. 139; no wording to match.

heldout.py: one table-valued label at a time freed, language model picks its value: restores 5 of 25 (letters-only pool) and 2 of 25 (with syllables). The method cannot infer values of unmatched shapes with 45% of tokens unknown.

cribs.py: 19 content words (denaro, stantie, cavalli, Cosimo, Fiorentini, Milanesi, ducati, Montevarchi, conte, compagnie, gente, pace, guerra, duca ...) searched against the table-decoded runs, unknown sign = 1-2 letters, 300 order-shuffled controls: none spelled out. Content words are nomenclator signs, not spelled.

f. 134: the seven glossed runs transcribed sign by sign (texts/f134_signs.md). Glosses give: run 6 'le compagnie in' = le co m pa g (table values, spelled); run 3 ends with the bar-o-bar-o sign, glossed 'del duce', not Veneziani as in the 1454 tables; Fiorentini = V with a circle on each top corner; 'gente d'arme in Toscana' written in 11 and 8 signs.

Bar-o-bar-o = duca in 1446 (not Veneziani): gloss on f. 134 run 3 plus contexts on f. 139 ('adherirvi ala via del duca', 'al favor del duca', 'l'impresa contra .. duca') and the Duke's letter f. 145 of 1 Dec. Tentative, not tested against a control.

f. 139 re-read with the f. 134 values: Fiorentini (V with a circle on each top corner) located at L7, L23, L28, L36 (context 'che [Fiorentini] debiano hauer per male', L36); bar-o-bar-o read duca ('adherirvi ala via .. duca', 'al fauor de .. duca', 'adyutassi duca'). Positional test: the sign before duca is the o sign in 5 of 11 cases (base rate 6.6%, binomial p 4e-4); four runs end 'e X o duca' with X = @12 or @102, so X = l ('e lo duca'). Tentative; no control run on the substitution.

f. 139 relabelled with duca, Fiorentini and the 9-shape sign (@12/@102 unified) and rescored (relabel.py): stretch score of the table letters -2.204 (353 letters) -> -2.149 (456 letters) with @12 = l and duca/fiorentini as words; z 4.0 against 100 shuffled assignments of the table values. Single-sign scans over 55 candidate values: @12 (32 uses) best l (z 2.3 among the 55; next i); @101 (18 uses) best e (z 1.8, weak); other shapes <= 9 uses show no clear best. Control (hide a table sign, scan): signs with >= 16 uses come back at rank 1-2 (u, a, e, i, o); rarer ones do not (re, te, p, c, n rank 2-26), so only @12 is accepted (tentative) and @101 is not. Decoded runs then show 'e lo duca' six times, 'duca in', 'cento mila hor.', 'hauete che'. 487 of 788 run signs carry a value (62%); 301 unmatched or ambiguous. Rotated V at L5 (first sign, left-pointing triangle with circles on its right edge) looks like the Fiorentini sign turned on its side; unconfirmed. No sign always follows the same clear function word (checked, none repeats twice).

outcome.method_basis: Leaves identified and glosses read; no key value assigned and no text read yet; work in progress.
outcome.notes: In progress: f. 139 transcribed twice; table letters fit (z 3.9, no-space model) and give readable fragments; f. 134 glosses give duca (bar-o-bar-o) and Fiorentini (V with two circles); with them the clear context of f. 139 reads as a letter urging Sforza to the Duke's side, but the cipher runs are still mostly unread (word signs and unmatched shapes). Relabelled with duca, Fiorentini and l (@12, 9-shape): z 4.0 on the table letters, 62% of run signs valued, 'e lo duca' six times; 301 run signs unmatched. Solvers fail held-out controls.
